title: Sticky Parsnip Treacle Squares
tagline: Bonfire Night toffee flavours in a soft, spiced, parsnip-sweetened sponge.

ingredients.item: eating apple, grated with skin on
dark brown soft sugar (100g for the sponge, 75g for the sauce)
butter (100g for the sponge and greasing, 50g for the sauce)
black treacle (2 for the sponge, 1 for the sauce)

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Melt 100g butter. Use a little to grease a 20cm square tin, then line it with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs, 100g sugar, 2 tbsp treacle and the rest of the melted butter until smooth. Stir in the grated parsnips and apple.
Fold in the flour and ginger until just combined. Scrape into the tin, level the top and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile, melt 50g butter with 75g sugar, 1 tbsp treacle and the salt in a small pan. Simmer gently for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the cream and bubble for 3 to 4 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened. Take off the heat.
Rest the cake for 10 minutes, then cut into squares. Serve warm, drowned in the toffee sauce.
image_prompt: Square slices of dark golden-brown spiced sponge on a white plate, flecks of grated parsnip and apple visible in the crumb, covered in glossy amber toffee sauce pooling around the edges, with a jug of extra sauce and a spoon beside it.
alt_text: Squares of dark spiced parsnip sponge on a white plate, covered in glossy toffee sauce, with a small jug of extra sauce beside.
caption_hook: Parsnips in pudding sound odd until you remember carrot cake. They're sweeter, if anything. Would you try this by the bonfire, or is it strictly an indoor pudding?
